newsitem.title: ROMANIA: ROMANIA INFLATION SEEN RISING TO 97 PCT IN 1997.
newsitem.headline: ROMANIA INFLATION SEEN RISING TO 97 PCT IN 1997.

text.p: Romania expects year-on-year inflation to quicken to 97 percent this year from 56.9 percent in 1996, a government official said on Tuesday.
"The forecast for inflation was used to calculate the government offer for the wage indexation this year, which would cover around 75 percent of the expected price rises" the official told Reuters.

An overvalued local leu currency and overspending by former ruling leftists reignited inflation which surged to a year-on- year 56.9 percent last year, twice the level of 1995 and nearly triple a 20 percent target agreed with the International Monetary Fund.
The government estimated that inflation would be 41 percent in the first quarter of 1997, led by January's fuel price hike and expected electricity and food price rises.
But inflation will calm down towards year's end, the official said.
Central bank governor Mugur Isarescu on Monday said that price liberalisation, expected to occur in the first half of 1997, would trigger what he called a "corrective inflation."

He said the reform package which the new coalition government is discussing with the IMF and the World Bank was aimed "at slashing inflation to an annualised rate of under 30 percent in the second half of 1997."
"That means a monthly inflation of around 2.0 percent in the last months of 1997," he said.

The government is expected to announce the reform package later this week, at the end of talks with the IMF and World Bank seeking to gain a combined $1.0 billion in fresh credits to underpin reforms.

Romania has made progress in cutting inflation from near-hyperinflation of the immediate post-communist years. Inflation fell to 27.8 percent in 1995 from 61.7 in 1994 and almost 300 percent in 1993. -- Mirela Eremia, Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
